chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Justice is sweeter than the water that quenches the thirsty. How extensive is justice when it is applied in a matter, even if it is little.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of justice in Shia ethics according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of water for the thirsty to illustrate that justice (al-'Adl) is the most fundamental and refreshing virtue for both rulers and the ruled. This hadith underscores the Shia principle that justice is not merely a legal obligation but a spiritual necessity, where even a small act of fairness carries immense weight and sweetness, reflecting the divine attribute of equity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The justice is sweeter than the water poured upon the thirsty one. How extensive is the justice when justice is done in it (a matter), and even though it may be little’.
en.sarwar: 20. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Justice is sweeter than water is for a thirsty man. How vast is justice when it is practiced in an issue even though it would be very little!”
